questions.question_text:
Find $x$ on the straight line.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.9]\usetikzlibrary{angles,quotes}\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\coordinate (A) at (2.5,0);\coordinate (B) at (-2.5,0);\coordinate (C) at (127:2.2);\draw (B)--(A);\draw (O)--(C);\pic[draw,"$127^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.65cm,angle eccentricity=1.8]{angle=A--O--C};\pic[draw,"$x$",angle radius=0.9cm,angle eccentricity=1.7]{angle=C--O--B};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Subtracts 127 from 190 rather than from the straight-angle total of 180.
Reverses the subtraction and calculates $127^{\circ}-90^{\circ}=37^{\circ}$, using a right-angle total instead of $180^{\circ}$.
Subtracts 127 from 360 by using the angles-at-a-point total.

questions.question_text:
Three angles share a straight line.
Find $y$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.9]\usetikzlibrary{angles,quotes}\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\coordinate (A) at (2.6,0);\coordinate (B) at (-2.6,0);\coordinate (C) at (36:2.2);\coordinate (D) at (94:2.2);\draw (B)--(A);\draw (O)--(C);\draw (O)--(D);\pic[draw,"$36^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.5cm,angle eccentricity=2]{angle=A--O--C};\pic[draw,"$58^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.73cm,angle eccentricity=2]{angle=C--O--D};\pic[draw,"$y$",angle radius=0.98cm,angle eccentricity=1.7]{angle=D--O--B};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Adds the two known angles and reports their total as the missing angle.
Subtracts only 58 degrees from 180 and ignores the 36-degree sector.
Subtracts only 36 degrees from 180 and ignores the 58-degree sector.

questions.question_text:
Find $b$ on the sloping straight line.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.9]\usetikzlibrary{angles,quotes}\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\coordinate (A) at (25:2.5);\coordinate (B) at (205:2.5);\coordinate (C) at (107:2.2);\draw (B)--(A);\draw (O)--(C);\pic[draw,"$82^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.63cm,angle eccentricity=1.9]{angle=A--O--C};\pic[draw,"$b$",angle radius=0.9cm,angle eccentricity=1.7]{angle=C--O--B};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Completes 82 to 90 degrees as though the line formed a right angle.
Subtracts 82 from 190 instead of the half-turn total.
Uses 360 degrees as the total for the two angles on one line.

questions.question_text:
A signpost makes an angle of $112^{\circ}$ with one direction of a straight kerb.
What angle does it make with the other direction?

options.why: Subtracts 112 from 190 instead of from 180 degrees.
Uses a right-angle total and reverses the subtraction to calculate $112^{\circ}-90^{\circ}=22^{\circ}$.
Subtracts 112 from a full turn instead of a half turn.

questions.question_text:
Three adjacent angles on a straight line are $19.5^{\circ}$, $47.25^{\circ}$ and $x$.
Find $x$.

options.why: Reports the sum $19.5^{\circ}+47.25^{\circ}=66.75^{\circ}$ instead of subtracting it from $180^{\circ}$.
Calculates $180^{\circ}-47.25^{\circ}$ and ignores the $19.5^{\circ}$ angle.
Calculates $180^{\circ}-19.5^{\circ}$ and ignores the $47.25^{\circ}$ angle.
Calculates the complement $90^{\circ}-88.5^{\circ}$ instead of the supplement.
Subtracts $88.5^{\circ}$ from a full turn of $360^{\circ}$ instead of $180^{\circ}$.
Adds $88.5^{\circ}$ to $180^{\circ}$ instead of subtracting it.
These adjacent angles total 180 degrees and can form a straight line.
The remaining angle can be 45 degrees, making the total 180 degrees.
The two adjacent right angles total exactly 180 degrees.

questions.solution_text: Angles on one side of a straight line total $180^\circ$. In B, $150^\circ+50^\circ=200^\circ$, so it cannot represent a straight line. The other diagrams can total $180^\circ$.
